title: Fast final assembly for long talking-head videos
what_it_does: Builds the final MP4 for a 10-30 minute talking-head video with ffmpeg instead of rendering every frame in Chrome: captions (pop or clean, in the brand's colours and fonts from frame.md) are drawn once per state as transparent stills by HyperFrames and shown by ffmpeg; cards are rendered once on a transparent ground (WebM with alpha) and overlaid at their times; audio is loudness-normalised to -16 LUFS with true peak <= -1 dBTP in the same pass. Also writes an SRT and a YouTube chapters.txt (validated against YouTube's rules), and measures what it made.
when_to_use: When the video is longer than about two minutes, or when render time matters. Feed it the cut.mp4 and cut.words.json from silence-cut (made from a normalized copy). For short pieces with rich motion, the HyperFrames composition path of the captions and overlay-cards parts is fine. Not for footage that is not constant frame rate: run normalize first.
needs: hyperframes (the studio's pinned binary, for the caption stills and the cards)
notes: Overlay path: HyperFrames renders WebM with alpha (`--format webm` is transparent), ffmpeg decodes it with libvpx-vp9 and overlays; no splice needed. ffmpeg's ass/subtitles filter was not used: the Homebrew ffmpeg 9.0.2 here has no libass (nor drawtext), so captions are stills (no pop-in animation, the spoken word is accent-coloured and enlarged statically). Measured on a 46 s real phone clip: 80 caption stills in 19 s, 2 cards in 46 s (mostly Chrome start-up), x264 veryfast about 3 CPU-seconds per video second.
